question: Does the command refactor preserve Click command handling while exposing schema retrieval only through the leading form?

findings.description: SchemaDispatchGroup relies on Click's private _protected_args field to identify an ordinary missing command.
findings.analysis: The dispatch works today, but _protected_args is an internal Click detail rather than a supported integration boundary. A private sentinel command can let Click retain its own no-command behaviour while the dispatcher handles only the leading schema route.
findings.recommendation: Replace the private-field check with a sentinel-based dispatch path and retain the existing CLI behaviour tests.
findings.rationale: Remove the unnecessary dependency on Click internals while preserving the leading-only schema dispatch contract.

dispatch.outcome: The planned dispatcher will use a private sentinel route instead of Click's private argument state.

findings.description: Pending activity and settings requirements refer to the removed `ghbot schema` command.
findings.analysis: Both pending changes require a packaged JSON schema but describe its retrieval using the removed subcommand. An implementer following either requirement would document an invalid command form.
findings.recommendation: Update both requirements to name the supported leading `ghbot --schema` form.
findings.rationale: Keep pending requirements consistent with the supported schema retrieval interface before their implementation begins.

dispatch.outcome: Updated the command-refactor contract and both pending requirements to use the leading schema form.

recommendations.rationale: The sentinel dispatch removes the Click-internal dependency while preserving the specified schema forms and ordinary command parsing.
The follow-up corrects every pending schema-retrieval reference and keeps the command-refactor plan consistent with the delivered interface.
